question: Construct the matrix $I=[a_{ij}]$ of order $3\times3$ defined by $a_{ij}=1$ when $i=j$ and $a_{ij}=0$ when $i\ne j$, and use direct matrix multiplication with $$B=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\0&4&5\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}$$ to establish that $I$ acts as the identity matrix for multiplication on both sides of $B$.
explanation:
Formation of the Identity Matrix

According to the given rule, diagonal entries have $i=j$ and are therefore equal to $1$, while all non-diagonal entries have $i\ne j$ and are equal to $0$. Hence, $$I=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$$ which is the identity matrix of order $3$.

Left Multiplication

Now, $$IB=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\0&4&5\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}$$ Multiplying rows of $I$ by columns of $B$, we obtain $$IB=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\0&4&5\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}=B$$

Right Multiplication

Similarly, $$BI=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\0&4&5\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$$ Multiplication gives $$BI=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\0&4&5\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}=B$$ Thus, $IB=BI=B$. Therefore, the constructed matrix $I$ acts as the identity matrix for multiplication on both sides of the matrix $B$.
